title: Variables & Types
description: Bindings, mutability, types, casts, and constants in Rust
theory:
## Variables in Rust

Rust binds names with `let`. Bindings are **immutable by default**; use `let mut` when the value may change.

### Bindings

```rust
let name = "Alice";
let age: i32 = 25;
```

### Basic types

Common scalar types include `i32`, `i64`, `u32`, `f64`, `bool`, `char`, and `&str` / `String`.

### Type ascription and inference

Types are often inferred; you can write them explicitly (`let x: f64 = 10.0;`).

### Shadowing

You may redeclare with `let` to shadow a name (even changing type).

### Constants

```rust
const MAX_SCORE: i32 = 100;
```

### Tuples for multiple values

```rust
let (a, b) = (5, 10);
```

Use the same exercise ids as the Go course for easy cross-reference.

exercises.title: Declare a binding
Multiple bindings
exercises.description: Bind `name` to `"Rust"` and `version` to `1.85` (f64). Print them on one line separated by a space.

exercises.title: Numeric cast
exercises.description: Bind `x` to `100` as `i32`. Cast to `f64` into `y`. Print `y` (should print `100` without decimals for this exercise use integer-looking output).
hints: println!("{}", y as i32); // or print y with {:.0}

exercises.title: Printing default values
exercises.description: Print `i32` zero, `f64` zero, an empty string, and `false`, space-separated (mirrors Go’s zero-value demo).

exercises.title: Constants
exercises.description: Define constants `MAX_SCORE` and `MIN_SCORE` as `100` and `0`. Print both.

exercises.title: Grouped let
exercises.description: Use a single `let` with a tuple pattern to bind `host`, `port`, `debug` from `("localhost", 8080, true)`. Print all three.

exercises.title: Swap with tuple destructuring
exercises.description: Bind `a` and `b` to `5` and `10`. Swap using tuple assignment `(a, b) = (b, a);`. Print `a` and `b`.
